title: Applied ML evals: integrated playbook for eval harness, prompt sets, onboarding, guardrails, quantization, and regression triage
author: Daniel Kim
content:
Summary

This playbook provides an integrated, operational reference for Applied ML teams at Redwood Inference to onboard models, maintain curated prompt sets and benchmarks, run the eval harness, apply quality guardrails, adopt quantization profiles, and perform regression triage. It is intended for ML engineers, applied researchers, and SREs who manage production inference quality and cost tradeoffs.

Scope and goals

- Scope: evaluation and quality processes for any model intended for serving on Redwood (hosted, dedicated, private). Includes model onboarding checklist, how to build and maintain prompt sets, running and interpreting the eval harness, quantization profile guidance, and an incident-driven regression triage workflow.
- Goals: reproducible evals, measurable quality SLOs, clear rollout gates, fast regression root-cause and mitigation, and cost-aware quantization recommendations.

Key definitions

1. Eval harness — the standardized test runner and metric collection pipeline used by Applied ML to evaluate model outputs against curated prompt sets. Produces per-prompt and aggregate metrics, and stores results in the eval datastore.
2. Prompt set — a curated collection of input prompts and expected behaviors (gold labels, soft criteria, or acceptance heuristics) used to measure a model's capability for a target workload.
3. Quality guardrail — a configured rule that triggers review/fallback when a metric crosses a defined threshold (e.g., hallucination rate > 2% for customer-facing generation).
4. Quantization profile — a pre-tested configuration describing bit-width, operator fallback rules, and calibration steps used to reduce model size/latency with measured quality deltas.

Ownership and SLAs

- Primary owner: Applied ML (owner_team: engineering).
- Secondary owners: Serving Runtime (for kernel/latency interactions), Eng SRE (for infra-run SLOs), Customer Success (for customer-facing regression handling).
- Expected SLOs for eval process:
  - Eval run turnaround: 90% of full-model runs complete within 4 hours (on standard eval infra).
  - Regression triage time-to-first-action: <= 2 business hours for high-severity regressions (customer-impacting).

Eval harness: onboarding and runbook

Overview
- The eval harness is a Dockerized runner that accepts a config YAML, prompt set, and model spec, then performs batched requests (simulated at target request shapes), records outputs, and computes metrics. All runs write to the eval datastore with run_id and provenance.

Quick start CLI

- Example: run a full evaluation locally or on CI
  - docker run --rm -v $PWD:/data redwood/eval-harness:stable 
    --config /data/eval-config.yaml --prompt-set /data/prompt-set.json --model-spec gpt-open-1.0 --run-id mytrial-20270601

Required YAML fields (eval-config.yaml)

- model_spec: string
- prompt_set_path: string
- batch_size: int
- temperature_schedule: list
- metrics: list (e.g., ["accuracy", "bleu", "hallucination_rate", "toxicity_score"])
- compute_profile: {cpu_cores: int, gpu_type: string}  # include in YAML as plain text table (see examples)

Interpreting core metrics

- Accuracy / exact match: when a gold label is available.
- BLEU / ROUGE: for structured text tasks; use with caution for short answers.
- Hallucination rate: proportion of outputs flagged by heuristics or human review as unsupported. We target <= 1.5% for internal-assistant workloads and <= 2% for public generation.
- Latency p95: end-to-end token generation p95 under test traffic shape.

Prompt sets and benchmark management

Principles for prompt sets

1. Representative: reflect customer traffic distributions (length, slot types, instruct vs chat).
2. Versioned: every prompt set has semantic versioning (vX.Y).
3. Labeled: include gold labels where feasible; otherwise include clear acceptance heuristics and human-review tags.
4. Diversity: include edge cases, adversarial examples, and common customer patterns.

Prompt set metadata (JSON example)

- id: string
- version: string (semver)
- owner: team/email
- tags: list
- created_at, last_updated
- description
- prompts: list of {id, text, expected: {gold_text|heuristic|human_flag}}

Benchmark lifecycle

1. Create: owner curates prompt set and defines pass/fail thresholds per metric.
2. Validate: run on staging model variants + baseline; inspect top failure modes.
3. Approve: reviewers sign off (applied-ml lead + product owner).
4. Use: the set is added to nightly runs and pre-rollout gating.

Model onboarding guide (minimum viable checklist)

1. Pre-onboarding: confirm license and artifacts, model_id, model format (HF, GGUF, safetensors), and initial performance claims.
2. Eval harness run: baseline run against the selected prompt sets (target workloads). Capture metrics and artifacts.
3. Quantization pass: run the recommended quantization profiles (see Quantization section) and capture delta table (size, latency, metric deltas).
4. Safety scan: run toxicity classifiers, PII detectors, and safety heuristics.
5. Load test: perform throughput and latency profiling under production-like batching shapes.
6. Rollout policy: define canary % and fallback variants.

Model onboarding gate criteria (example)

- Quality: no metric regressed > 3% absolute above baseline for high-priority benchmarks.
- Hallucination: must be <= baseline + 1%.
- Latency: p95 must be within service SLA for the target tier.
- Security/compliance: license OK and model artifacts signed.

Quality guardrails: configuration and operational playbook

Guardrail types

- Threshold guardrails: numeric thresholds on eval metrics (e.g., hallucination_rate, toxicity_score).
- Behavioral guardrails: heuristic checks on output length, presence of forbidden tokens, or disallowed content classes.
- Regression guardrails: relative checks against a pinned control model (e.g., cannot drop > 2% in intent accuracy).

Example guardrail table

- Name: Hallucination-Assistant-Gen
- Metric: hallucination_rate
- Threshold: 0.015
- Severity: high
- Action: block rollout, notify applied-ml + oncall, revert to fallback model

Guardrail enforcement flow

1. Eval run triggers guardrail checks.
2. If violated, the run is flagged and an automatic rollback policy is activated for canaries.
3. Pager/Slack notification to applied-ml and SRE on high severity.
4. Create a triage ticket with run artifacts and top failing prompts attached.

Quantization profiles and guidelines

Principles

- Measure every change: for each quantization profile, run eval harness on baseline prompt sets and record deltas.
- Conservative defaults for customer-facing models: prefer 8-bit/4-bit mixed strategies with operator fallbacks for attention and LayerNorm.
- Fallback rules: allow per-op float fallback when known-quality regressions appear.

Recommended profiles (summary table)

- profile_id: q8_default
  - bitwidth: 8
  - operator_fallbacks: attention: float32, layernorm: float32
  - expected_size_savings: ~2x
  - recommended_for: latency-sensitive internal workloads

- profile_id: q4_mixed
  - bitwidth: 4 with grouped quantization
  - operator_fallbacks: attention: float16, layernorm: float32
  - expected_size_savings: ~3.5x
  - recommended_for: high-throughput batch workloads where small quality delta is acceptable

- profile_id: q4_aggressive
  - bitwidth: 4 aggressive, reduced calibration steps
  - operator_fallbacks: none (best effort)
  - expected_size_savings: ~4x
  - recommended_for: research experiments only

Quantization validation checklist

1. Run calibration on representative data (>= 5k tokens across contexts).
2. Run eval harness with same prompt sets as baseline.
3. Generate delta report: metrics, latency, memory, and qualitative failure examples.
4. If any high-severity metric regresses beyond gate, enable per-op fallback and rerun.

Regression triage playbook

Severity levels

- P0 (Critical): customer-facing regression causing user-visible incorrect outputs, data exposure, or major outage. Action: immediate rollback.
- P1 (High): significant metric regression on primary benchmark (>3% absolute) or sustained increase in error rates. Action: 2-hour triage and mitigation.
- P2 (Medium): minor regressions or non-customer-facing metrics. Action: 3-day investigation window.

Triage steps (numbered)

1. Detection: metric alert or customer report triggers a triage ticket. Attach eval run_id and failing sample list.
2. Quick assess (15-–30 min): run the eval harness on the previous good model and the current model over the same prompt set to confirm delta.
3. Scope: determine impact surface (which customers/routes are affected, traffic %).
4. Hypothesis generation: consider recent changes (model version, quantization profile, runtime kernel changes, prompt-engineering changes).
5. Mitigation: choose immediate action—rollback canary, enable a fallback model, or apply guardrail to block responses.
6. Root cause analysis: deeper log and tensor inspection, compare logits for failing prompts, and consult kernel/quantization teams if numeric drift is suspected.
6a. If quantization-related, run the quantization validation checklist and try operator fallbacks.
7. Resolution and follow-up: create a postmortem for P0/P1 incidents, update prompt sets or guardrails as needed, and add regression test to nightly suite.

Artifacts to attach to triage ticket

- eval run_id and link to run artifacts
- failing prompt examples (top 25) and model outputs
- delta report (CSV/JSON) with per-metric change and p-values where applicable
- relevant configs (quantization profile, model spec, runtime kernel version)

Nightly automation and continuous monitoring

- Nightly runs: all production models run against the canonical prompt sets nightly. Results stored in the eval datastore and compared against pinned baselines.
- Automated alerts: guardrail violations open a ticket and notify owners.
- Regression ingestion: all triage findings feed into the prompt set maintenance backlog (owners must address recurring failure classes).

Example config and artifacts (YAML / JSON snippets)

- eval-config.yaml example:
  model_spec: gpt-open-1.0
  prompt_set_path: /prompt_sets/assistant_general_v1.json
  batch_size: 16
  temperature_schedule: [0.0, 0.7]
  metrics: ["accuracy", "hallucination_rate", "latency_p95"]

- quantization-profile.json example:
  profile_id: q4_mixed
  bitwidth: 4
  operator_fallbacks: ["attention:float16", "layernorm:float32"]
  calibration_samples: 5000

Governance and review cadence

- Owners must review prompt sets quarterly and update failing examples and thresholds.
- Any change to a canonical prompt set requires an approval PR from Applied ML and at least one reviewer from Product or Customer Success if the set is customer-facing.
- Quantization profiles that are promoted to production must have an associated audit: evaluation artifacts, delta report, and a rollout plan.

Appendix: common failure modes and mitigations

- Mode: Regressions after kernel changes
  - Symptom: numeric drift in logits, small but systematic quality drop.
  - Mitigation: run targeted unit tests comparing logits on golden inputs, revert kernel or enable numeric-stable fallback.

- Mode: Hallucination spikes with longer context lengths
  - Symptom: hallucination_rate increases when context length > 1024 tokens.
  - Mitigation: extend prompt set coverage, update caching behavior, and consider seq-length-specific kernels or prefix caching.
